DNA damage activates the spindle assembly checkpoint through the action of ATR/ATM, independently of the kinetochore.
the SAC is activated by DNA damage and that the DNA damage checkpoints Mec1 and Tel are required for SAC activation.
the DNA damage checkpoint arrests cells in anaphase by activating the SAC, independently of the kinetochore, and that ATM and ATR inhibit anaphase independently of Chk2 and Chk1.

understanding the mechanism of action of DNA damage checkpoint and spindle assembly checkpoint.
the mechanisms by which cells sense and respond to DNA damage and chromosome missegregation.
the mechanisms that regulate the cell cycle.

the DNA damage checkpoint and SAC work together, in a manner dependent on ATR/ATM, but independent of kinetochores, to inhibit the cell cycle.
DNA damage activates the SAC in an ATR/ATM-dependent manner, but that the SAC is kinetochore-independent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA damage activates SAC in an ATM/Atr- dependent manner, independently of the kinetochore.
DNA damage can activate the SAC in an ATR-ATM-dependent, but kinetochore-independent manner.
ATM and ATR are required for the SAC in an ATR- and ATM-dependent manner, independently of the kinetochore.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spindle assembly checkpoint is activated in response to DNA double strand breaks in an ATM/ ATR-dependent manner, independently of the kinetochore, and that this activation is important for the maintenance of genomic stability.
the SAC can be activated by DNA damage, independently of the kinetochore, and that this activation requires ATM and ATR.
the SAC can be activated by DNA damage in a manner that is independent of the kinetochore and that this activation requires both ATM and ATR.
